title: Best Bread Makers UK
short: Six bread makers compared on the loaves they actually produced, from a £70 machine for seasoned bakers to a 68-programme premium model and a gluten-free specialist.
intro: A bread maker's real test is the loaf it bakes on every setting. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, where the team made several loaves in each machine and tested every setting, from basic white and wholewheat to seeded and gluten-free, plus extras such as crust types, proofing, kneading and jam-making. Expert Reviews' guide dates from July 2023, so prices are as reviewed and may have changed.

products.name: 23620 Compact Breadmaker
products.best_for: Small households and kitchens trying bread making for the first time
products.key_spec: 12 programmes, three loaf sizes, three crust settings, 55-minute quick bake, 13-hour delay timer
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this dinky machine perfect for small households and kitchens, able to handle classic white, gluten-free or a wholemeal baguette across 12 settings, three loaf sizes and three crust settings. A quick bake option makes a classic loaf in 55 minutes and a 13-hour delay timer lets you wake to fresh bread, though it has no fruit and nut dispenser.
pros: 12 settings, three loaf sizes and three crust settings
Affordable for a first bread maker

products.name: Touchscreen Bread Maker
products.best_for: Buyers who want a large touchscreen and a multi-function machine
products.key_spec: 12 programmes, 1kg/1.25kg/1.5kg loaves with two kneading blades, LED touchscreen, 60-minute keep warm, also makes cakes, jam and yoghurt
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this multi-purpose machine easy to follow at a glance thanks to a large, easy-to-use LED touchscreen, with presets for different loaves plus cakes, jam and yoghurt. Two kneading blades let you choose a 1kg, 1.25kg or 1.5kg loaf, and it keeps the finished loaf warm for 60 minutes, though it has no fruit and nut dispenser.
pros: Also makes cakes, jam and yoghurt
products.search: Lakeland Touchscreen Bread Maker and More

products.name: The Custom Loaf
products.best_for: Serious bakers who want maximum control over every stage of the programme
products.key_spec: 68 programmes, custom recipes, large screen and twist knob, fruit and nut dispenser, collapsing paddle, about 3 hours for a standard white loaf
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this celebrity-chef-endorsed machine lets you tweak recipes or create whole new ones, with a collapsing paddle so there's no hole in the bottom of the loaf. The reviewer's loaves from the recipes came out well, though they were lower, like bakery loaves, than the tall sandwich loaves many are used to, and the results weren't radically different to other models.
pros: Almost endless tinkering with custom programmes
Collapsing paddle avoids a hole in the loaf
cons: Loaves come out lower, like bakery loaves, rather than tall sandwich loaves
Results not radically different to other models despite the price
products.search: Sage by Heston Blumenthal The Custom Loaf bread maker

products.name: Fastbake Cooltouch Breadmaker
products.best_for: Buyers who mainly want a quick, excellent white loaf on a tight budget
products.key_spec: 29 programmes, standard white loaf in about 2 hours 53 minutes, viewing window (unlit)
products.summary: Expert Reviews found it more than makes up for its lack of looks by turning out an excellent white loaf quickly, making it exceptional value if that's mostly what you bake. The reviewer struggled a little to get wholemeal loaves as good, the controls are fiddly and wobbly, reflecting the cheaper build, and the baking chamber isn't lit, so you'd need a torch to check through the window.
cons: Struggled a little with wholemeal loaves
Controls are a little fiddly and wobbly

products.name: EK4189 Digital Bread Maker
products.best_for: Experienced bread makers who want plenty of customisation
products.key_spec: 15 settings including wholewheat, gluten-free, sweet bread and French loaves, dough setting, about 3 hours for a white loaf
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the fastbake, basic and wholewheat settings all produced a soft loaf with a crusty exterior, while the dough setting kneaded and proved dough to soft, pillowy perfection. Unusually it comes with no recipes or printed instructions, which must be downloaded from Salter's website, and the instructions aren't the clearest, so beginners should steer clear.
pros: Soft loaves with a crusty exterior on tested settings
Dough setting kneads and proves well
cons: No recipes or instructions in the box, must be downloaded
Unclear instructions, not ideal for a first bread maker

products.name: Fully Automatic Breadmaker
products.best_for: Bakers who want gluten-free, brioche and wholewheat loaves with automatic dispensers
products.key_spec: 32 programmes including four gluten-free, automatic yeast and nut/raisin dispensers, 13-hour delay timer, 0.6kg maximum loaf
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a feature-rich machine with 32 automatic programmes, including four for gluten-free loaves, that adds extra ingredients and yeast at the right time via automatic dispensers. It also handles cakes, pizza dough and jam through manual settings, but the loaf is on the small side at a maximum 0.6kg, a little smaller than a standard shop loaf.
pros: Also makes cakes, pizza dough and jam
products.search: Panasonic fully automatic breadmaker gluten free

guide.q: Is a bread maker cheaper than buying bread?
guide.a: Expert Reviews says you can expect to pay just over half the cost of a similarly sized shop-bought loaf, or more if you experiment with nuts, seeds or gluten-free flour, and you control the ingredients for a preservative-free loaf. It takes time to recoup the machine's price, and homemade bread goes stale faster than shop-bought.

guide.q: What size bread maker do I need?
guide.a: If you finish a whole loaf in a few days, consider a 2lb tin. Households of one or two are better with a smaller 1 or 1.5lb pan, since homemade bread has no preservatives and needs eating sooner. Also check the machine's own footprint, and note the Panasonic here makes only a 0.6kg loaf.

guide.q: Do I need an automatic fruit and nut dispenser?
guide.a: Only if you bake fruit or seeded loaves more than occasionally. Machines without one, like the Russell Hobbs and Lakeland here, beep when it's time to add ingredients, so you need to be there. The Sage and Panasonic here dispense them automatically at the right point in the cycle.

guide.q: What flour and ingredients do I need?
guide.a: Usually strong bread flour, salt, sugar, oil or butter, water and bread-machine yeast. Supermarket own-brand strong flour is fine for white loaves, but some machines need expensive 'very strong' flour for a decent wholemeal loaf, so check reviews. Cool the loaf on a wire rack before slicing.
